blocks.text:
In the morning, a transfer takes you from your hotel to Punta Arenas airport for the flight to King George Island in Antarctica.

Your guide meets the group on arrival. The island programme includes:

- Villa Las Estrellas, the Chilean settlement on King George Island.
- The Russian Orthodox Church at Bellingshausen Station.
- A Zodiac trip to Ardley Island and a visit to a penguin colony.
- Navigation towards Collins Glacier.

After approximately five hours, weather permitting, you are scheduled to fly back to Punta Arenas. A transfer takes you to your hotel on arrival.

**The entire programme is subject to weather conditions.** Local conditions in Antarctica determine whether flights, landings and individual itinerary activities can take place.

blocks.text:
**Dates:** 3–21 February / 10–15 March

King George Island is home to research stations and the Chilean settlement of Villa Las Estrellas. During the land programme, you will learn about life at Antarctic bases, visit the Russian Orthodox Church at Bellingshausen Station, take a Zodiac to Ardley Island and its penguin colony, and head towards Collins Glacier.

The entire trip is subject to weather conditions. Two types of aircraft and different group sizes are used for different departures:

- Beechcraft King Air 300: minimum 5 passengers, maximum 6 per flight.
- Bae-146 200: minimum 20 passengers, maximum 35 per flight.

## What you will see along the way

On the way to Antarctica, the aircraft flies over the southern tip of South America and the Drake Passage. The flight ends on King George Island, the starting point for the Antarctic part of the trip and an area with many research bases.

On the island, you will see Antarctic landscapes, some local wildlife and the places where research station staff live and work throughout the year.
